01 Machine Quotas & Resource Allocation

  • Machine Definition: A "Machine" on usectl represents a Kubernetes namespace (kdeploy-<name>) paired with a defined resource quota allocation (vCPU, RAM, block storage) and subscription billing plan. A machine holds no application code directly.
  • Pod Workloads: Workloads ("Pods") execute within a Machine's resource envelope. Pod deployments that exceed the Machine's vCPU or RAM quota preflight checks will be rejected until idle resources are cleared or the Machine plan is upgraded.
  • Storage Limits: Persistent block storage allocations across all volumes in a single project are hard-capped at an absolute ceiling of 250 GB.

02 High Availability, Local Storage & Service SLA

  • Single-Node Local Storage: Default volume claims use local-path storage bound directly to a single physical node disk via node affinity. Single-pod stateful workloads bound to local disks will experience temporary downtime if the underlying host node becomes unavailable.
  • High Availability Addons: High availability and failover protection require multi-instance deployments. Dedicated PostgreSQL instances deploy as 2-instance CloudNativePG clusters (primary + streaming replica) with automated failover. Dedicated NATS instances deploy as a 3-node RAFT cluster; clients must explicitly configure streams with Replicas: 3 to enable stream failover across broker losses.

03 Billing, Grace Periods & Machine Archiving

  • Billing Cycles: Subscriptions are billed on a recurring basis via Stripe.
  • Lapsed Billing & Grace Period: If an invoice payment fails or a subscription lapses, the Machine enters a 7-day grace period. Warning notifications are sent 3 days prior to grace period expiration.
  • Automated Archiving: Upon expiration of the 7-day grace period, all active workloads inside the Machine and its sibling group namespaces are automatically scaled to 0 replicas, and the Machine is marked as archived.
  • Deployment Suspension: Deployments targeting archived Machines are rejected with an HTTP 409 Conflict status until billing is reinstated.

04 Account Security & Session Revocation

  • Refresh Token Rotation: Access tokens expire after 24 hours. Refreshing tokens consumes the active refresh token and issues a new token pair. Presenting a previously consumed refresh token indicates potential credential compromise and will result in the immediate revocation of the entire token family session.
  • Acceptable Use: Users are prohibited from attempting lateral network probes across tenant namespaces, bypassing NetworkPolicies, or launching unauthorized compute tasks on unprivileged build nodes. Violations result in immediate account termination.
